author_claim: Paul cites Hosea 2:23 and 1:10 in Romans 9:25-26 specifically to establish that God's "vessels of mercy" include believing Gentiles alongside a believing Jewish remnant.
short_quote: it seems clear that Paul was citing these verses to establish the point that God's "vessels of mercy" include Gentiles.
qualification: Paul does not introduce the Hosea quotes with the words "Now concerning the Gentiles," but the structural bracket between Rom 9:22-24 and 9:30-31 demands this conclusion.
notes: Tanner 2005:98. Supporting Gentile inclusion as vessels of mercy.

author_claim: In Romans 9:25, Paul quotes from a Greek rendering of Hosea 2:23, reversing the clause order and changing the verb to "I will call" (καλέσω) to emphasize divine election and match Romans 9:24.
short_quote: Paul quoted from a Greek rendering of Hosea and the fact that he reversed the order of the clauses
qualification: Paul switched Hosea's "I will say" to "I will call" matching Romans 9:24; reversing clause order places this verb at the beginning of the composite quotation.

author_claim: In Hosea's original eighth-century B.C. historical context, Hosea 1:10b and 2:23 pertained strictly to the northern kingdom of Israel being disowned and later restored, containing no reference to Gentiles.
short_quote: Nothing in the context of these passages makes reference to Gentiles, nor did Hosea imply that the fulfillment of these promises would be with Gentiles.
qualification: Hosea 1:10a alludes to the sand-of-the-sea promise of the Abrahamic Covenant made specifically to ethnic Israel.
notes: Tanner 2005:100. Original Hosea context restricted to northern kingdom of Israel.

author_claim: Paul's application of Hosea 1:10b and 2:23 to Gentile believers affirms that the conversion of Gentiles is a direct, partial fulfillment of Hosea's prophecy rather than a mere analogy or general principle.
short_quote: verses 25-26 affirm that the conversion of Gentiles is a direct fulfillment of Hosea's prophecy (though not the complete fulfillment).
qualification: It is a direct fulfillment, but not the complete or exhaustive fulfillment, which still includes the future restoration of ethnic Israel.
notes: Tanner 2005:102. Rejection of mere analogy; direct partial fulfillment.

author_claim: The mechanism enabling Gentiles to experience the Hosea status change from "not My people" to "My people" is their full participation in the New Covenant promised in Jeremiah 31:31-34, Ezekiel 36:24-28, and Hosea 2:18.
short_quote: It was the New Covenant that made it possible for the Jewish remnant to become "the people of God." The context of Hosea (particularly the mention of a "covenant" in Hosea 2:18) confirms this. Since it was the New Covenant that made it possible for Gentiles to become part of the church, the "not my people" in the Hosea passages ultimately had Gentiles in view.
qualification: Participation in the New Covenant conveys spiritual status as "the people of God," but does not transform Gentile believers into "Israel" or "spiritual Israel."
notes: Tanner 2005:110 (and pp. 106-107). New Covenant as the theological bridge for Gentile inclusion.

author_claim: Paul does not teach that the church has replaced Israel or that Israel has forfeited her covenant promises; national, land, and kingdom promises remain reserved for ethnic Israel at Christ's return.
short_quote: Paul was not operating by some new theological dictum whereby Israel no longer meant Israel. Instead he had come to understand the Gentile aspect of fulfillment.
qualification: Distinguishes shared spiritual blessings enjoyed by New Covenant participants from specific physical and geographic promises reserved for ethnic Israel.
notes: Tanner 2005:103 (and pp. 96, 110). Rejection of supersessionism; Israel still means Israel.

author_claim: Paul clarifies in Romans 9-11 the crucial distinction between ethnic Israel in unbelief and the believing Israelite remnant, demonstrating that God's covenant promises to Israel have not failed.
short_quote: In Romans 11 the apostle clarified this distinction between ethnic Israel in unbelief and the believing Israelite "remnant." God's covenant promises to Israel have not failed, because God will fulfill them with the believing remnant.
qualification: True Israel consists of the believing remnant within ethnic Israel; God's word has not failed because the promises were never intended to apply indiscriminately to all physical descendants without faith.
notes: Tanner 2005:96. Romans 9:6 true Israel and remnant theology.

author_claim: Paul reversed the order of the clauses in Hosea 2:23 to stress the "My people" aspect of the promise and God's sovereign call to them, aligning the quotation with Romans 9:24.
short_quote: reversed the order of the clauses (perhaps to stress the "My people" aspect of the promise and God's "call" to them).
qualification: Reversing the clause order allows the verb καλέσω ("I will call") to stand at the head of the composite Hosea quotation.
notes: Tanner 2005:99. Clause reversal placing "My people" first to stress divine election call.
